Title: Tournament Report - The Stranger Among Us - Columbus, OH 1/11/02

Messages.Author: John Bell
Messages.Body:
The Stranger Among Us - Columbus, OH 1/11/02

Great turnout with 27 total players, lot of craziness throughout the
tournament from what I understand. Two Balimore Purge decks, each
with 2 Table Wins, both making the finals; lot of stealth bleed decks
from what I saw/heard - at least one Setite S&B and 4 Malk decks (1
old school and 3 dementation based).

Round 1
-------
4 player table for me, I was fortunate with my weenie potence deck, I
had an Assamite prey and a Salubri/!Ventrue deck as my predator. Each
time that my prey was able to get to range on me, I had a Thrown
Sewer-Lid to greet them. I actually got bled more by my grandpredator
than by my predator, fortunately for me, his Setites had no way to
deal with Immortal Grapple and Fame+Humanitas came in real handy.
When it was down to me and my predator, it wound up being 3 or 4 more
turns, when he finally ran out of Fortitude combat defense, it was
over - I think the round lasted about 40 minutes for our game. 4 VPs:
table sweep.

Round 2
-------
5 player table, not nearly the spectacular results for me, sneak &
bleed predator and grand-predator - so time was very limited for me
from the whistle. Only notable things for me this round were hitting
poor Lucinde for 9 of her 10, Disarming her, then getting the blessing
from the other Ventrue at the table to let KoKo partake of some fine
dining...even the solitary VP I "earned" was going after a Fame'd
Mustafa Rahman, it took 4 rush actions, a) because my prey kept waking
and blocking b) because I had no combat in hand - I finally got him
with an unblocked Harass when he was at 1 blood and so was I, hands
for 1, press from Harass, hands for 1. Result 1 VP and ousted next
turn.

Round 3
-------
5 player table and another time when it was obvious (to me anyway)
that I had removed some of the combat teeth in the deck. Largish
!Brujah prey and Dominate/Potence/Fortitude predator, built around
Lazverinus, made my combat machine look somewhat anemic. I never had
more than 3 ready minions, I was forced to block each of Lazverinus'
Governs and if I somehow did influence out a 4th minion, I was rushed
by my prey. Not often that I'm used to this deck being rushed - it
was certainly a new experience for me ;) Oh highlight of the round
was my predator believing he was ousted (didn't think he could
generate +1 intercept to stop a bleed) when I pointed out he had 2
untapped minions and one with a Starshell Grenade Launcher. He tapped
his SGL minion, blocked with Lazverinus and proceeded to grab the
table win. I thought it was pretty smooth, he sat at 1 pool for
probably 6 - 8 turns, before going on to take 4 of the 5 VPs. My
results 0 VP.

Finals
------
Once again I managed to skate into the finals somehow, and as per
usual, no one wanted to sit near me. 2 decks featuring Balimore Purge
made the finals, interestingly enough. 3 of the 5 finalists were from
Cincinnati (including myself) and one of those decks was a Ventrue
deck that had 3 Table Wins and almost swept each of his tables (I
could be wrong, but I think he missed 1 VP at 1 table). The Finalists
were Doug Brindley of Columbus going first and playing dementation
Malks/!Malks, myself second playing weenie Potence, Matt Flint of
Cincinnati playing a Vitel/Lasombra Balimore Purge deck, Dave Setty of
Cincinnati playing a Freak Drive-million-actions-a-turn Ventrue deck,
and Nate Williams of Newark playing a vicious Balimore Purge/Protect
Thine Own/Graverobbing deck - a true work of art.

Unfortunately for my prey he never really got into the game, I had too
many minions, way too fast and he only drew 2 Obedience. Everyone
seemed intent on stopping Nate's Purge deck, aside from me. The
largest minion I had for most of the finals was Lupo/KoKo/Paul
DiCarlo, so losing one of them to a Purge was not a huge deal for me.
Probably the two biggest key moments in the finals were the 2 Sudden
Reversals I played: the first was to blow up a Fame my prey played
cross-table on Nate's Etrius (I'm not down with contesting my ONLY
Fame in the deck and it went a long way for goodwill on later deals).
The next Sudden Reversal was against my prey's Auspex card played on
my grandprey's Arika...would have put her out of Purge reach. I
finally set the terms that Nate had to burn her on his turn, I didn't
want to see any Graverobbing/cross-table rescuing, etc - he carried
out his end and it was one less minion I had to worry about when I got
to Dave. When I got through my first prey, Dave's Ventrue gave me
much more difficulty with a solid mix of Fortitude and Majesty to keep
me at bay. By this time I played a Haven Uncovered on Etrius, and
things were looking very good. Nate did oust Doug and looked to have
a dangerous amount of Dominate, but it either didn't come up, or it
wasn't a focus other than to Graverobbing. An Ancient Influence by my
prey looked to buy himself enough time and put Nate out of reach, but
then some of my Computer Hackings came up and I still had 6 minions.
When it was down to Nate and myself, he waited for me to put Etrius in
the dirt, then conceeded; I had enough minions to bleed him for 2 a
turn and block all of his actions. Result was 4 VP and the table,
Nate with 1 VP.

>could be wrong, but I think he missed 1 VP at 1 table).

Nearly - only one sweep here.
First table was me, a !Brujah cel/pot combat deck as my prey, an
obf/dem stealth-bleed with some combat (Coma, disguised Rowan Ring and
such) as his prey, and a Giovanni bruise/bleed as his prey (my
predator). My predator and prey either didn't have or didn't draw
enough grapples to keep me from getting away (didn't help that my prey
was having to use them on the Malkavians) and they couldn't prevent me
from bloating. The Giovanni were ousted first, but the Malkavians
couldn't stop me before I ousted the Brujah and I won after 2 of the 3
Malks were burned (one by an Archon Investigation, one by diablerie
after a Kiss of Ra.)

Second round my prey was a pot/for/dom bruise-bleed deck, his prey was
a set-1 Nosferatu combat deck, and his prey (my predator) was a set-3
Nos deck (with some combat, some stealth-bleed, and some intercept).
This table could have given me trouble, as the bruise-bleed deck might
have been able to beat up my minions while ousting the 2 Nos decks
(both players seemed not to be very experienced). Unfortunately for
him, I went third, and started to influence out Democritus, he went
fourth and brought up Emerson Bridges, and then Democritus proceeded
to Govern out my copy of Emerson. He was not able contest Emerson
against Democritus's special ability, and was fairly quickly ousted,
and I proceeded to sweep.

Third table, my prey was a Samedi combat deck, his prey was Doug
Brindley's obf/dem stealth-bleed deck, his prey was another obf/dem
stealth-bleed deck, and my predator was an AUS weenie/Salubri bleed
deck. My predator was kept busy with bleeds against him, and the
Samedi didn't draw enough combat cards (which was good, because I
wasn't drawing enough Majesty). I finally eliminated the Samedi, Doug
eliminated the other Malkavians, and then I eliminated Doug, by which
time I had an enormous amount of pool and outlasted the Salubri.

> The Finalists
>were Doug Brindley of Columbus going first and playing dementation
>Malks/!Malks, myself second playing weenie Potence, Matt Flint of
>Cincinnati playing a Vitel/Lasombra Balimore Purge deck, Dave Setty of
>Cincinnati playing a Freak Drive-million-actions-a-turn Ventrue deck,
>and Nate Williams of Newark playing a vicious Balimore Purge/Protect
>Thine Own/Graverobbing deck - a true work of art.
>
>Unfortunately for my prey he never really got into the game, I had too
>many minions, way too fast and he only drew 2 Obedience.

If I recall correctly, Marcus Vitel was dropped by the Purge and
diablerized, and Matt didn't last long after that (he brought out
Gratiano, who was killed, and then was ousted). I wasn't too happy, as
it put the Potence hordes on me much sooner than I had hoped, and I
never got the chance to make Vitel the Ventrue Justicar.

>Everyone seemed intent on stopping Nate's Purge deck, aside from me.

Imagine that.

>Probably the two biggest key moments in the finals were the 2 Sudden
>Reversals I played: the first was to blow up a Fame my prey played
>cross-table on Nate's Etrius

That was huge - he might not have played a Purge with a famous Etrius,
and if he had done it anyway the pool loss might have let me oust him.

>The next Sudden Reversal was against my prey's Auspex card played on
>my grandprey's Arika...would have put her out of Purge reach.

I would have lost a minion anyway, but the loss of +2 bleed and
difficulty passing votes over Etrius kept me from ousting Nate.

>Result was 4 VP and the table, Nate with 1 VP.

And again, congratulations on your victory.

Make sure if anyone else in the surrounding states is reading this bs,

enjoy the slim competition chumps. And plus the prince of Newark (Mark
Loughman), Columbus (Jay Kristoff), and Cininnatti (John Bell) are
more than hospitable. They are well practiced in the ways of the 5th
Tadition. Anyway...

In response to Johan's suggestion...

can we see the deck lists for the two purge decks? (this is about the
only instance that i've heard of a purge deck making the finals)

Normally I wouldn't even think about listing my stuff. However, after
reading Mr John Bell's illustrious comments about my (QOUTE) "Nate

Williams of Newark playing a vicious Balimore Purge/ProtectThine

Own/Graverobbing deck - a true work of art." (end quote)...Don't
forget stealth bleed, and extra cheese on that order (With a side of
fries). I have decided to list it anyway. So, for the first and last
time ever, I will age my smelly cheese before your very eyes.
But this deck does still go down in flames to weenie potence, so you
could substitute in or out a few votes to make people burn pool equal
to # of minions they control. That will stomp the weenie potence in
the nuts. Anyway...

For another variant, take out 8 to 10 cards and replace them with 4-5
Blood Fury, and 4-5 Bone Spur, and watch fortitude/Immortal Grapple
decks go to the dirt.

Crypt is this see... 4 Etrius, 3 Cameron, 3 Aaron Dugan, 2 Mustafa
Rahmon

Masters (16)-Just the basics-... 4 Blood Doll, 1 Political H.G., 1
Academic H.G., 3 Vulnerability, 4 Chantry, 2 Secure Haven ( for the
Cameron or his toady), and 1 Arcane Library

Actions (15)-The cheese ages- 7 Baltimore Purge, 4 Graverobbing, 4
Protect Thine Own

Modifiers (24)-overkill is a must- 6 Forgotten Labyrinth, 8 Lost in
Crowds,
6 Cloak the Gatherings, and 4 elder impersonation.

Reactions (21)-What's that smell?- 8 Wakes w/eve freshnes, 8
Deflections, and 5 Telepathic Misdirections

Combat (14)-The usual crap- 8 Flesh of Marble, and 6 earth meld.

Tremere Chantry is the best stuff around with the purge. Just see the
looks on peoples faces when I put Etrius in the dirt from my own Purge
on untap phase, and then he pops out like stay fresh muffins on my
maser phase. Then ideally you Vulnerability someone, Protect Thine Own
another non-cam that is ready (just one more casualty), Graverob
someone with a Mustafa or Cameron, and Diablerize anyone else left. It
is really easy to control the votes when the only voter left is
Etrius, take it from me. And he is already an 11 cap, and can Purge
anyone he damn well plaeases right away.

Previous to the Columbus Tournament, I had the deck together for 2 and
a half months, and had only played it 2 times. But it usually makes
for a 20-30 minute 4 player game. And a 25-40 minute 5 player. In a 5
player, it is always nice to help your grand-predator as much as
possible. 5 people on 1 is never good, but 2 on 3 os great. That way
your predator is shut down, you smoke 2 people to your left, and then
destroy your original grand-preator for the win, after you play him
like a puppet on a string. You know, the usual.

Make sure you excersize this deck with extreme prejudice against
everyone at the table. Don't make deals, just smoke vamps. Talk is
cheap. Just be the only guy at the table with vamps, and bleed
everyone to death. Oh, and by the way, this deck is not a one trick
pony. It can just plain bleed and send bleeds to your prey at will. I
purposely didn't play some (5-6) Purge in the last 2 tables, just to
make it game. I like to bleed people out nice and slow. Sometimes I
can be so old fashioned. Me and John Bell just ran the last table. Big
ups to Bell for the assist in taking out Brindley and cinching me 2nd
place

And one last item I have to discuss...about this "Matt Flint of
>Cincinnati playing a Vitel/Lasombra" (so-called) "Balimore Purge
deck"

I smoked this deck 2 times 2 times, and must say it is a pale
imitation. Matt is my man, but to be the man, you got to beat the man.
And Mark Loughman is the man. So get to beating him fellas. He was
talking about you guys. All nice, but he was talking nonetheless. I
hear Matt has all but stripped the contents of my deck to play for
himself now. How incredibly weak. But oh well. That is why I posted
this first, and last crappy deck. (Because every deck I play is BS.
Everybody knows it.) I don't need some dude claiming my stuff as his
own. So now you know. I hope your Jyhad experience has been enhanced
by the great knowledge I spew forth. So speaks the
polish...@hotmail.com. Feel free to reply (with fan mail, or hate
mail) I don't care which. Just don't send me your deck ideas, as I'm
sure they are stale as a year old cracker.

Thanks for running a tournament in Anderson IN this weekend, that was
fun. Thanks to Jay, Mark, and Bell. I will be running a tournament
soon at Newark, OH. Come one and all, and bear witness to a small
comic shop in the middle of nowhere that will host a 25-30 man
tournament. And get your butts handed to you. I will be running the
tournament, and the smack-talk. So my prince can play this time. Plus
I need to take a break, and come up with something original. I will
post details soon, and I hope Bernie can make it this time.

Thanks for listening. Nate/Archon of Newark

P.S. I am soon listing my trades on the Communal Haven, since the
Succubus Club is gone. Under the name polishgenius. Later
